pairs.question: Quid ergo inter fulgurationem et fulmen interest?
pairs.answer: Fulguratio est late ignis explicitus, fulmen est coactus ignis et in impetum iactus.
pairs.derivation: Author poses the question and answers it himself. Dropped the framing word 'Dicam' that stands between question and answer ('Quid ergo inter fulgurationem et fulmen interest? Dicam. Fulguratio est...'). Answer ends at the first full stop; what follows ('Solemus duabus manibus...') is an illustrative digression, cut.

pairs.question: Quare inaequalia sunt?
pairs.answer: Quia et ipse ictus inaequalis est.
pairs.derivation: Part of Anaximander's reported catechism on thunder. 'Tonitrua, inquit, sunt nubis ictae sonus' precedes; the next clause is the standalone Q&A 'Quare inaequalia sunt? Quia et ipse ictus inaequalis est.' Clean interrogative directly answered. Stops at the full stop before the next question 'Quare et sereno tonat?'.

pairs.question: Quare et sereno tonat?
pairs.answer: Quia tunc quoque per crassum et scissum aera spiritus prosilit.
pairs.derivation: Next item in Anaximander's catechism. Interrogative directly answered with 'Quia...'. Ends at the full stop before 'At quare aliquando non fulgurat et tonat?'.

pairs.question: Quid est fulmen?
pairs.derivation: Closing item of Anaximander's catechism. Direct definitional question and answer; the sentence is the last in the section, so the answer runs to the period.

pairs.question: Quare oblique fertur?
pairs.answer: Quia spiritu constat, spiritus autem obliquus est flexuosusque, et quia natura ignem sursum uocat, iniuria deorsum premit.
pairs.derivation: Author's own question (subject is the lightning, fulmen, from the preceding sentence) answered immediately with 'Quia...'. Editorial dashes around 'spiritus autem obliquus est flexuosusque' removed (they bracket an explanatory aside that is part of the answer's grammar). Ends at the full stop; the next sentence 'incipit autem obliquum esse iter...' elaborates and is cut.

pairs.question: Quare frequenter cacumina montium feriuntur?
pairs.answer: Quia opposita sunt nubibus et e caelo cadentibus per haec transeundum est.
pairs.derivation: Self-contained authorial question answered directly. The whole section is this single Q&A, so the answer runs to the period.

pairs.question: Quare fulmen subitum apparet nec continuatur assiduus ignis?
pairs.answer: Quia celere mirique motus simul et nubes rumpit et aera incendit, deinde desinit flamma motu quiescente.
pairs.derivation: Author's question (dropped the leading connective 'At', normalized 'Quare' to capital) answered directly with 'Quia...'. Ends at the first full stop; the continuation 'Non enim assiduus est spiritus cursus...' explains further and is cut.
